title: Loudoun Electrical Infrastructure Comprehensive Plan Amendments
summary: Loudoun County's notice opens a local planning process for high-voltage transmission corridors and related comprehensive-plan policy in a jurisdiction carrying concentrated data-center load.
key_findings: The county initiated review of comprehensive-plan amendments addressing electrical infrastructure and high-voltage transmission corridors.
The process makes local land-use authority and corridor routing visible alongside state utility regulation.
The notice is an upstream planning record and does not identify a final policy, route, easement, or completed asset.
why_it_matters: It shows that power delivery in a compute corridor is partly a local land and routing problem, not only a demand forecast or state-utility decision.
ftfn_relevance: Adds a local land-use rail to the Northern Virginia conversion stack.
Links transmission planning to public process, route selection, and project delivery.
Provides a record path from proposed policy to final action and named infrastructure.
evidence_limits: Process initiation is not final county policy.
A corridor concept is not land control, a certificate, construction, or energization.
The notice does not establish customer-specific capacity or service.
